newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Expert on U.S. named SKorean foreign minister.
newsitem.headline: Expert on U.S. named SKorean foreign minister.

text.p: President Kim Young-sam on Wednesday named his chief foreign policy advisor, Yoo Chong-ha, as South Korea's new foreign minister, a presidential spokesman said.
Yoo replaces Gong Ro-myung, who tendered his resignation on Tuesday, citing poor health.
"The new minister is one of the country's well-known experts on U.S. affairs," a Foreign Ministry official said.

Yoo, 60, a career diplomat, was a senior official at South Korea's embassy in Washington and headed the Foreign Ministry's U.S. Bureau before serving as ambassador to Sudan, Belgium, the European Community and the United Nations.
He was also the vice foreign minister between 1990 and 1992 before being named the chief presidential advisor for foreign and security affairs in 1994.
Gong, who has high blood pressure, has been admitted to a Seoul hospital, a Foreign Ministry spokesman said.
"President Kim accepted Minister Gong's resignation," presidential spokesman Yoon Yeo-joon said, adding that Gong had "offered to resign because of aggravating health."
Gong is the second senior minister to be removed from Kim's cabinet in less than a month.
Kim dropped defence minister Lee Yang-ho on October 17 after fierce criticism of the military for failing to intercept an intruding North Korean submarine.

On Tuesday, South Korean troops killed two North Koreans who had been on the run since the submarine landed 26 agents after it ran aground off the eastern city of Kangnung on September 17, a military spokesman said. One of the North Koreans remains at large, one has been captured and the rest have been shot dead.
Lee now faces trial on charges of bribery. State prosecutors said he had admitted accepting 150 million won ($181,000) last year in connection with the government's purchase of military helicopters.
